hyps.why: Replacing none with a conv adds a whole path, a larger gain than replacing other ops.
Edge 4 reads node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is zero and a conv on edge 2 acts on nothing.
Adding a conv path into the output gains more than swapping an existing op.
Adding a conv path from none gains more than replacing an existing op.
Edge 0 none kills node 1, so a conv there revives a whole branch.
The shortcut at node 3 reduces the marginal value of an extra conv path.
A direct skip into node 3 makes the longer conv path less necessary.
Adding a conv where there was no edge adds a new path into node 2.
Adding a path where none existed gains more than swapping an existing op.
